proofs.proof_tex:
Expanding the covariance definition and using
\(w_j(a)=\sum_{(g,t)\in O}a_{g,t}b_{(g,t),j}\) gives, term by term,
\[
 a^{\prime}\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}a
 =\frac{\sigma^2}{N}\left[
 \sum_t\left\{\sum_{g\in G_t}\frac{a_{g,t}^2}{q_g}
 +\frac{A_t(a)^2}{q_{>t}}\right\}
 +\sum_j\frac{w_j(a)^2}{q_j}\right]
 =\frac{\sigma^2}{N}E(a). \tag{8}
\]
This uses the block formula for \(V\), the definition of \(b\), and the
proved score-covariance lemma.  If \(\sum_tA_t(a)=1\), then
\[
 \mathbb E_x[a^{\prime}Z]-f_T
 =\sum_tA_t(a)(f_t-f_T)+\sum_t v_t(a)^{\prime}u_{\cdot,t}. \tag{9}
\]
The Holder condition bounds the first sum in (9) by \(LH(a)\).  For every
\(c\in\mathbb R\), calendar centering gives
\(q^{\prime}u_{\cdot,t}=0\), and hence
\[
 |v_t(a)^{\prime}u_{\cdot,t}|
 =|(v_t(a)-cq)^{\prime}u_{\cdot,t}|
 \le B\|v_t(a)-cq\|_1. \tag{10}
\]
Taking the infimum in (10), summing over \(t\), and combining with (9)
proves the bias bound.  Equation (8) proves the standard-deviation formula.

For the slow channel, take the single date \(t=T-k\) and set
\(a_{g,t}=q_g/Q_k\) for \(g\in G_t\), with all other coefficients zero.
Then \(A_t(a)=1\), \(H(a)=(k/T)^\beta\), and
\[
 D(a)\le R_k/Q_k\le (C_q/c_q)k/(T-k). \tag{11}
\]
Direct substitution in (8) gives
\[
 \sum_{g\in G_t}\frac{a_{g,t}^2}{q_g}=Q_k^{-1},
 \qquad \frac{A_t(a)^2}{R_k}=R_k^{-1}, \tag{12}
\]
while
\(w_j=-q_j/Q_k\) on \(G_t\) and \(w_j=q_j/R_k\) on \(C_t\).  Therefore
\[
 \sum_j\frac{w_j^2}{q_j}=Q_k^{-1}+R_k^{-1},
 \qquad E(a)=2(Q_k^{-1}+R_k^{-1}). \tag{13}
\]
Balanced cohorts, \(k\le\delta T\), and \(T-k\ge(1-\delta)T\) imply
\(Q_k\asymp1\) and \(R_k\asymp k/T\).  Equations (11)--(13) prove the
slow-channel upper bound and its contribution
\(Bk/(T-k)+\sigma\sqrt{T/(Nk)}\).

We next give the fast construction.  First suppose \(2k<T\), and choose two
disjoint reverse-date blocks, each of cardinality comparable to \(k\), inside
\([3k/2,2k]\).  If \(2k\ge T\), then \(k\asymp T\); because
\(m\le\delta T<T\), the interval \([m,T-1]\) contains two separated blocks
of cardinality at least \(c_\delta T\asymp k\), and we use those instead.
Put constant totals \(A_r\) on
each block and choose the two block totals to solve
\[
 \sum_rA_r=1,\qquad \sum_r A_r/R_r=0. \tag{14}
\]
Because balanced cohorts give \(R_r\asymp r/T\), the determinant of this
two-by-two system is bounded away from zero after the common \(T/k\) scale is
removed.  Thus
\[
 \max_r|A_r|\le C/k,\qquad \sum_r|A_r|\le C. \tag{15}
\]
For equal shares define \(P_s=\sum_{r>s}A_r/r\).  Equation (14) makes
\(P_s=0\) before the first block, and the support choice gives
\[
 |P_s|\le C/k,qquad \sum_s|P_s|\le C,qquad \sum_sP_s=1. \tag{16}
\]
For balanced shares the same statements hold with
\(P_j=q_j\sum_{t<j}A_t/q_{>t}\).  Distribute the row masses in (16) over
eligible dates and allocate each residual column mass proportionally over an
eligible subblock of cardinality at least \(c k\).  The two blocks are
separated precisely so that every such row and column has at least \(ck\)
eligible partners.  This finite transportation construction has the prescribed
column sums \(A_r\), the row sums
\[
 \sum_{t\ge j}a_{j,t}=q_j\sum_{t<j}\frac{A_t}{q_{>t}}, \tag{17}
\]
and the bounds
\[
 |a_{j,t}|\le C/k^2,\qquad
 \sum_{(j,t)\in O}|a_{j,t}|\le C_F,
 \qquad
 \sum_{t,j}\frac{a_{j,t}^2}{q_j}\le CT/k^2. \tag{18}
\]
To verify (18), each of the \(O(k)\) row and column margins is
\(O(1/k)\), it is spread over at least \(ck\) cells, and
\(q_j\asymp1/T\); hence every allocated cell is \(O(1/k^2)\), and summing
\(O(k^2)\) squared cell entries gives
\(O(T/k^2)\).  The same proportional allocation bounds its total variation
by the sum of the absolute row and column margins, which is a constant.
Equation (17) is exactly \(w_j(a)=0\).  Equations (14)--(18) also give
\[
 H(a)\le C_H(k/T)^\beta,qquad D(a)\le C_F,qquad
 \sum_t\frac{A_t(a)^2}{q_{>t}}\le CT/k^2. \tag{19}
\]
Thus (8), (18), and (19) prove the fast-channel upper bound.

For its converse, let \(H(a)\le C_H(k/T)^\beta\) and
\(\sum_tA_t(a)=1\).  Choose \(\lambda>1\) with
\(C_H\lambda^{-\beta}\le1/2\).  Then
\[
 \sum_{T-t>\lambda k}|A_t(a)|\le1/2,
 \quad\text{so}\quad
 \sum_{T-t\le\lambda k}|A_t(a)|\ge1/2. \tag{20}
\]
Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz and balanced cohorts give
\[
 \sum_t\frac{A_t(a)^2}{q_{>t}}
 \ge
 \frac{\left(\sum_{T-t\le\lambda k}|A_t(a)|\right)^2}
 {\sum_{r\le\lambda k}R_r}
 \ge c_0T/k^2, \tag{21}
\]
where the last inequality uses
\(\sum_{r\le\lambda k}R_r\le Ck^2/T\).  This proves (21) whenever
\(\lambda k<T\).  If \(\lambda k\ge T\), then \(k\ge T/\lambda\), and
Cauchy--Schwarz over all score cells gives
\[
 \sum_t\sum_{g\in G_t}\frac{a_{g,t}^2}{q_g}
 \ge\frac{(\sum_tA_t(a))^2}{\sum_t\sum_{g\in G_t}q_g}
 \ge\frac1T\ge\frac{T}{\lambda^2k^2}. \tag{22}
\]
Thus the same lower order holds in the complementary case.  Since the left
sides of (21) and (22) are summands of \(E(a)\), this proves the fast-channel
lower bound.

Finally, applying the bias bound and (8) to the slow and fast arrays, and
choosing the one with the smaller bound at each \(k\), gives the displayed
hybrid inequality.  The baseline-covariance obstruction theorem proves the
last sentence.  None of these steps supplies the missing lower interpolation
between the two deviation budgets, so the proof does not identify the
diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\) with the exact modulus.

By the proved score-covariance lemma, the statistical experiment is exactly
\(Z\sim\mathcal N(Kx,\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}})\).  Let
\(e=(\mathbf 1_T,0)\).  Adding any multiple of \(e\) preserves the Holder
increments, the cohort bound, and calendar centering, so \(e\) is a lineality
direction of \(2\mathcal M_{T,m}\).  Moreover,
\(Ke=\mathbf 1_{|O|}\ne0\) and \(\ell(e)=1\).  Positive definiteness of
\(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\) therefore implies
\[
 d_e:=\|Ke\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}>0. \tag{22}
\]
If a modulus maximizer at radius \(r>0\) had Mahalanobis norm strictly less
than \(r\), adding a sufficiently small positive multiple of \(e\) would
remain feasible and strictly increase \(\ell\), a contradiction.  Also,
adding \((s-r)e/d_e\) to an optimizer at \(r<s\) proves
\(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(s)\ge
\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)+(s-r)/d_e\).  Hence the constraint is
active and the right derivative is positive at every radius; in particular,
\(1\in\mathcal R_+\).

Write \(\omega=\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}\),
\(s_1=\omega'(1)\), and \(b_1=\{\omega(1)-s_1\}/2\).  Concavity,
monotonicity, and \(\omega(0)\ge0\) give
\[
 0<s_1\le\omega(1)-\omega(0)\le\omega(1),
 \qquad 0\le b_1\le\omega(1)/2. \tag{23}
\]
The exact-bias assertion in the proved total-modulus rule and the Gaussian
variance calculation yield
\[
 \sup_x\mathbb E_x[(\widehat\theta_1-\ell(x))^2]
 =b_1^2+s_1^2\le\frac54\omega(1)^2. \tag{24}
\]
Because the defining sequence \(r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}\) approaches the infimum
over \(\mathcal R_+\), and radius one is admissible, (24) proves the two upper
inequalities after taking \(\liminf_j\).  The first of those inequalities also
holds because \(R^\star\) is the infimum over all measurable estimators.

For the lower bound, let \(x^-_1,x^+_1\) be the canonical modulus endpoints
at radius one.  Their target separation is \(\omega(1)\), and their Gaussian
mean separation has squared Mahalanobis norm one.  If \(P_-\) and \(P_+\)
denote their laws, the Gaussian likelihood-ratio identity gives
\[
 \chi^2(P_+,P_-)=e^1-1.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \|P_+-P_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\frac12\sqrt{e-1}. \tag{25}
\]
For any estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), classify the endpoint according to
which of \(\ell(x^-_1)\) and \(\ell(x^+_1)\) is closer to
\(\widetilde\theta\).  On a classification error the squared estimation error
is at least \(\omega(1)^2/4\).  The sum of the two testing errors is at least
\(1-\|P_+-P_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Consequently
\[
 \max_{x\in\{x^-_1,x^+_1\}}
 \mathbb E_x[(\widetilde\theta-\ell(x))^2]
 \ge\frac{\omega(1)^2}{8}
 \left(1-\frac12\sqrt{e-1}\right). \tag{26}
\]
Both endpoints are in \(\mathcal M_{T,m}\).  Taking the supremum over that
class and then the infimum over estimators proves the lower bound.  This
argument uses the exact covariance modulus only and therefore makes no claim
about the diagnostic calendar functional.

Fix \(j\), put \(r=r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\), \(b=b_r\), and \(s=s_r>0\).
The score-covariance lemma and the exact-bias and variance conclusions of the
total-modulus rule give, for every \(x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}\),
\[
 \frac{\widehat\theta_r-\ell(x)}s\sim\mathcal N(t_x,1),
 \qquad |t_x|\le b/s. \tag{27}
\]
For fixed \(c\ge0\), the function
\(t\mapsto\Pr\{|\mathcal N(t,1)|\le c\}\) is even and nonincreasing on
\([0,\infty)\): differentiating it for \(t>0\) gives
\(\phi(c+t)-\phi(c-t)\le0\).  The definition of
\(\operatorname{cv}_\alpha\) and (27) therefore imply the displayed uniform
coverage.  Measurability follows from the proved total-modulus rule.  The
factor \(1+j^{-1}\) affine half-length assertion is exactly the defining
inequality for \(r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\).

Let \(z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).  The triangle inequality shows that
\[
 \Pr\{|\mathcal N(t,1)|\le t+z_\alpha\}\ge1-\alpha
 \quad(t\ge0),
\]
so \(\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(t)\le t+z_\alpha\).  The lineality argument
in the minimax proof shows \(1\in\mathcal R_+\).  At radius one, (23) gives
\(b_1\le\omega(1)/2\) and \(s_1\le\omega(1)\).  Hence
\[
 2s_1\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b_1/s_1)
 \le2b_1+2z_\alpha s_1
 \le(1+2z_\alpha)\omega(1). \tag{28}
\]
The infimum-approaching property of \(r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\) and (28) prove the
upper expected-length bound; interval length is deterministic for each member
of this affine family.  The middle inequality follows because these intervals
are measurable and honest and thus are feasible in the definition of
\(\operatorname{EL}^{\star}_\alpha\).

For the converse, note that \(0<r_\alpha<1\) because
\(0<1-2\alpha<1\).  Let \(x^-_{r_\alpha},x^+_{r_\alpha}\) be the canonical
modulus endpoints and let \(P_-,P_+\) be their laws.  Their target separation
is \(\omega(r_\alpha)\), and the Gaussian likelihood-ratio calculation used
in (25) gives
\[
 \|P_+-P_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\frac12\sqrt{e^{r_\alpha^2}-1}
 =\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}. \tag{29}
\]
Let \(C(Z)\) be any measurable interval with uniform coverage at least
\(1-\alpha\).  Under \(P_-\), coverage of the lower endpoint has probability
at least \(1-\alpha\).  Coverage of the upper endpoint under \(P_-\) has
probability at least \(1-\alpha-\|P_+-P_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Therefore the
probability under \(P_-\) that the interval contains both endpoints is at
least
\[
 1-2\alpha-\|P_+-P_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \ge\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}. \tag{30}
\]
On this event, the interval property forces its length to be at least
\(\omega(r_\alpha)\).  Thus
\[
 \sup_x\mathbb E_x[\operatorname{length}C(Z)]
 \ge\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\omega(r_\alpha). \tag{31}
\]
Concavity and monotonicity of the modulus, together with \(\omega(0)\ge0\),
give \(\omega(r_\alpha)\ge r_\alpha\omega(1)\).  Substitution in (31) gives
the constant \(c_\alpha=(1-2\alpha)r_\alpha/2\).  Taking the infimum over
measurable honest interval-valued procedures proves the lower bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(q_j=1/T\), \(m=1\), and \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\).  Fix \(C_H,C_D<\infty\).  There is \(T_0=T_0(\beta,C_H,C_D)\) such that, for every \(T\ge T_0\), every coefficient array \(a\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_{t=1}^{T-1}A_t(a)=1,\qquad
 H(a)\le C_H(k/T)^\beta,\qquad
 D(a)\le C_Dk/(T-k)
\]
obeys
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^T\frac{w_j(a)^2}{q_j}\ge\frac1{16}.
\]
Consequently there is no constant \(C_E<\infty\), independent of \(T\), for which these three inequalities and \(E(a)\le C_ET/k^2\) hold simultaneously for all sufficiently large \(T\).  This is an obstruction to that four-inequality dual certificate; it does not assert that every bounded lift fails or that the exact nested modulus is not comparable to some closed-form rate.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(r=T-t\).  Choose a fixed \(\lambda>1\) so large that
\(\eta:=C_H\lambda^{-\beta}<1/8\), and then take \(T_0\) large enough that
\(\lambda k<T-1\), \(C_Dk/(T-k)<1/32\), and
\((T-\lambda k)/T>7/8\).  Define
\[
 J=\{t:1\le t\le T-1,\ T-t\le\lambda k\},
 \qquad E_0=\{j:j\le T-\lambda k\}.
\]
For every \(t\), choose a minimizer \(c_t\) of
\(c\mapsto\|v_t(a)-cq\|_1\), and put
\(\varepsilon_t=v_t(a)-c_tq\) and
\(D_t=\|\varepsilon_t\|_1\).  Such a minimizer exists because the displayed
function is continuous and coercive.  By the definition of \(D(a)\),
\(\sum_tD_t=D(a)\).  Since
\(A_t(a)-c_t=\sum_j\varepsilon_{t,j}\),
\[
 |A_t(a)-c_t|\le D_t. \tag{1}
\]
For \(t\notin J\), the Holder weight is at least
\((\lambda k/T)^\beta\).  The assumed bound on \(H(a)\) therefore gives
\[
 \sum_{t\notin J}|A_t(a)|
 \le (\lambda k/T)^{-\beta}H(a)
 \le C_H\lambda^{-\beta}=\eta. \tag{2}
\]
Using \(\sum_tA_t(a)=1\), (1), and (2),
\[
 \sum_{t\in J}c_t
 \ge 1-\eta-D(a). \tag{3}
\]

Let \(W_0=\sum_{j\in E_0}w_j(a)\).  If \(t\in J\), then every
\(j\in E_0\) satisfies \(j\le t\), and the definition of \(b\) gives
\[
 \sum_{j\in E_0}\sum_{g\in G_t}a_{g,t}b_{(g,t),j}
 =-\sum_{g\in E_0}a_{g,t}
 =-q(E_0)c_t-\sum_{g\in E_0}\varepsilon_{t,g}. \tag{4}
\]
For arbitrary \(t\) and \(g\in G_t\),
\[
 \left|\sum_{j\in E_0}b_{(g,t),j}\right|
 =\left|-\mathbf 1\{g\in E_0\}
 +\frac{q(E_0\cap C_t)}{q_{>t}}\right|\le1. \tag{5}
\]
Moreover, by (1),
\[
 \sum_{g\in G_t}|a_{g,t}|
 \le |c_t|+D_t\le |A_t(a)|+2D_t. \tag{6}
\]
Equations (3)--(6) and the triangle inequality imply
\[
 |W_0|
 \ge q(E_0)\{1-\eta-D(a)\}-\eta-3D(a). \tag{7}
\]
Here \(q(E_0)=(T-\lambda k)/T>7/8\).  The choices of \(\eta\) and
\(T_0\) make the right side of (7) larger than \(1/4\).  Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz now yields
\[
 \sum_{j=1}^T\frac{w_j(a)^2}{q_j}
 \ge \frac{\left(\sum_{j\in E_0}w_j(a)\right)^2}{q(E_0)}
 \ge\frac1{16}.
\]
Finally, \(T/k^2\to0\) for \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\).  Hence an
upper bound \(E(a)\le C_ET/k^2\) contradicts the last display for every
fixed \(C_E\) and all sufficiently large \(T\).  This proves exactly the
stated certificate obstruction.

added_lemmas.statement:
Determine the sharp dimension-free interpolation of
\(\Gamma_{T,m}(h,d)\) between the pooled slow channel and the
baseline-cancelled fast channel under balanced cohort shares.  In particular,
either prove a matching lower bound for the hybrid upper construction at every
intermediate deviation budget, with all constant dilations of \(h\) and
\(d\) stated explicitly, or construct a balanced-share counterexample.  The
answer must also decide whether unit-normalized claims such as
\(\Gamma_{T,m}((k/T)^\beta,k/T)\asymp T/k\) and
\(\Gamma_{T,m}((k/T)^\beta,1)\asymp T/k^2\) remain valid when \(m=k\), rather
than replacing the actual support constraint by an oracle date.
added_lemmas.justification: The exact coefficient program is computable, but a matching dimension-free lower interpolation is needed before any closed calendar phase diagram can be claimed.
added_lemmas.gap: The slow pooled geometry, the fast baseline-cancelled geometry, and the canonical obstruction leave the intermediate deviation budget unresolved.
added_lemmas.consumer: A resolution would convert the exact nested modulus into an explicit calendar-rate functional without assuming the missing transport inequality.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching lower Pareto interpolation for the exact nested-score energy under simultaneous Holder and cohort-deviation leverage constraints.
obligation.obstruction: The control-pool term gives the fast lower endpoint, while the early-cohort baseline functional gives a nonvanishing obstruction at one slow sequence; neither argument yields the uniform intermediate-deviation exponent.
obligation.attempted: Pooled one-date weights, separated reverse-date blocks with exact baseline cancellation, weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, and the early-cohort baseline functional were derived. They close the two feasible upper geometries, the fast lower endpoint, and the canonical impossibility certificate, but not the full interpolation.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact covariance identity and affine bias bound reduce the issue to the
finite convex program defining \(\Gamma_{T,m}\).  Pooled one-date weights give
energy \(2(Q_k^{-1}+R_k^{-1})\asymp T/k\) at deviation budget of order
\(k/(T-k)\).  A separated-block baseline-cancelling construction gives energy
of order \(T/k^2\) at a constant deviation budget, and the control-pool term
proves the matching universal lower bound of order \(T/k^2\).  For equal
shares, \(m=1\), and \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\), the baseline-Gram theorem
proves that simultaneous Holder leverage of order \((k/T)^\beta\), deviation
leverage of order \(k/(T-k)\), and energy of order \(T/k^2\) are impossible.
What remains is the matching lower interpolation between these two budgets.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every coefficient array \(a\),
\[
 a^{\prime}\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}a=\frac{\sigma^2}{N}E(a),
\]
and the affine statistic \(a^{\prime}Z\), when
\(\sum_tA_t(a)=1\), has worst-case absolute bias for \(f_T\) at most
\[
 L H(a)+B D(a).
\]
There are positive constants \(c_0,C_0,C_H,C_D,C_F\), depending only on
\(\beta,\delta,c_q,C_q\), such that, uniformly for
\(m\le k\le\lfloor\delta T\rfloor\), the following two geometries hold:
\[
 \Gamma_{T,m}\!\left((k/T)^\beta,C_Dk/(T-k)\right)\le C_0T/k,
 \tag{\text{slow channel}}
\]
and
\[
 c_0T/k^2\le
 \Gamma_{T,m}\!\left(C_H(k/T)^\beta,C_F\right)
 \le C_0T/k^2.
 \tag{\text{baseline-cancelled channel}}
\]
The slow-channel upper bound is attained by pooled one-date weights and has
exact energy \(2(Q_k^{-1}+R_k^{-1})\), where
\(Q_k=\sum_{g\le T-k}q_g\) and \(R_k=1-Q_k\).  The fast-channel upper bound
is attained by a data-driven coefficient array with \(w(a)=0\); it uses two
separated reverse-date blocks and the balancing equation
\(\sum_r A_r/R_r=0\).  Consequently one explicit affine procedure satisfies
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \left|\mathbb E_x[a^{\prime}Z]-\ell(x)\right|
 +\operatorname{sd}_x(a^{\prime}Z)
 \le C_0\min_{m\le k\le\lfloor\delta T\rfloor}
 \left[
 L(k/T)^\beta+\min\left\{
 \frac{Bk}{T-k}+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{T}{Nk}},
 B+\frac{\sigma\sqrt{T/N}}{k}
 \right\}\right].
\]
At the canonical equal-share sequence in the baseline-covariance obstruction
theorem, the slow-leverage constraints cannot be combined with energy of order
\(T/k^2\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim equates the exact nested modulus with the diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\) through an unspecified bounded right inverse. The proof establishes only the exact dual energy, bias map, two feasible covariance geometries, a fast-channel converse, and a canonical obstruction. The replacement removes the unproved equivalence and states the strongest proved operator-specific result.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Uniformly over the stated design range,
\[
 \frac{1-\frac12\sqrt{e-1}}8\,
 \omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2
 \le R^{\star}
 \le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \mathbb E_x\!\left[
 \{\widehat\theta_{r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}}-\ell(x)\}^2
 \right]
 \le\frac54\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2.
\]
Thus global minimax squared-error risk is comparable, with the displayed
numerical constants, to the exact modulus of the nested score operator.  The
candidate diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\), its minimizing depth \(k^{\star}\),
and a closed-form calendar phase diagram are not asserted to equal or be
equivalent to this exact modulus.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The exact Gaussian minimax comparison closes, but replacing \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\) by the diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\) requires the unresolved Pareto lower interpolation. The replacement retains the proved numerical constants and removes the unsupported phase diagram and nested homogeneous-rate claim.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(j\in\mathbb N\), \(C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\) is a measurable interval
and satisfies
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \Pr_x\{\ell(x)\in C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
exactly.  Its half-length is within the factor \(1+j^{-1}\) of the infimum
over the positive-standard-deviation affine modulus intervals in the stated
construction.  Put
\[
 r_\alpha=\sqrt{\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\}},
 \qquad c_\alpha=\frac{(1-2\alpha)r_\alpha}{2},
 \qquad z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\]
Then
\[
 c_\alpha\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)
 \le\operatorname{EL}^{\star}_{\alpha}
 \le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \mathbb E_x[\operatorname{length}C_{\alpha,j}(Z)]
 \le(1+2z_\alpha)\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1).
\]
The lower bound ranges only over measurable interval-valued procedures, as in
the definition of \(\operatorname{EL}^{\star}_{\alpha}\).  No closed-form
calendar-rate equivalence is asserted.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Exact coverage, affine-modulus optimality, and global expected-length comparison to the exact nested modulus are proved. The former comparison to \(\rho_{N,T,m}\) is not justified without the unresolved Pareto interpolation, so it is removed.

proposed.name: Baseline-cancellation Pareto frontier
proposed.construction:
For a coefficient array \(a=(a_{g,t}:(g,t)\in O)\), put
\[
 A_t(a)=\sum_{g\in G_t}a_{g,t},\qquad
 v_t(a)_j=a_{j,t}\mathbf 1\{j\in G_t\},
\]
\[
 H(a)=\sum_{t=1}^{T-m}|A_t(a)|\left(\frac{T-t}{T}\right)^\beta,
 \qquad
 D(a)=\sum_{t=1}^{T-m}\inf_{c\in\mathbb R}\|v_t(a)-cq\|_1,
\]
and
\[
 w_j(a)=\sum_{(g,t)\in O}a_{g,t}b_{(g,t),j},
\]
\[
 E(a)=\sum_{t=1}^{T-m}\left\{
       \sum_{g\in G_t}\frac{a_{g,t}^2}{q_g}
       +\frac{A_t(a)^2}{q_{>t}}
       \right\}
       +\sum_{j=1}^T\frac{w_j(a)^2}{q_j}.
\]
The baseline-cancellation Pareto frontier is
\[
 \Gamma_{T,m}(h,d)=\inf\left\{E(a):a\in\mathbb R^{|O|},\ 
 \sum_{t=1}^{T-m}A_t(a)=1,\ H(a)\le h,\ D(a)\le d\right\},
\]
with the infimum of the empty set equal to \(+\infty\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This finite convex optimization exposes the exact affine variables, leverage constraints, and covariance objective required by the operator-specific frontier.

proposed.name: Global minimax criteria
proposed.construction:
\[
 R^{\star}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \mathbb E_x[(\widetilde\theta(Z)-\ell(x))^2].
\]
Here the infimum is over measurable real-valued statistics.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{EL}^{\star}_{\alpha}
 =\inf_{C}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \mathbb E_x[\operatorname{length}C(Z)],
\]
where the infimum is over measurable interval-valued maps \(C\) such that
\(C(Z)\) is an interval almost surely under every \(x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}\) and
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \Pr_x\{\ell(x)\in C(Z)\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The honest-length lower bound uses the fact that every candidate is a measurable interval-valued map almost surely; the prior definition did not state this domain restriction.

proposed.name: Candidate diagnostic calendar functional
proposed.construction:
The candidate diagnostic calendar functional and one of its minimizing depths are
\[
 \rho_{N,T,m}=\min_{m\le k\le\lfloor\delta T\rfloor}
 \left\{L(k/T)^{\beta}+Bk/(T-k)+\sigma\sqrt{T/N}/k\right\},
\]
\[
 k^{\star}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{m\le k\le\lfloor\delta T\rfloor}
 \left\{L(k/T)^{\beta}+Bk/(T-k)+\sigma\sqrt{T/N}/k\right\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The formula remains a useful diagnostic, but its equivalence to the exact nested modulus is an open mathematical question rather than a definition or proved phase envelope.
The prose-only transport handle supplied no coefficients and smuggled the unproved right-inverse property; all surviving results use explicit coefficient constructions instead.

proposed.statement:
For every coefficient array \(a\),
\[
 a^{\prime}\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}a=\frac{\sigma^2}{N}E(a),
\]
and the affine statistic \(a^{\prime}Z\), when
\(\sum_tA_t(a)=1\), has worst-case absolute bias for \(f_T\) at most
\[
 L H(a)+B D(a).
\]
There are positive constants \(c_0,C_0,C_H,C_D,C_F\), depending only on
\(\beta,\delta,c_q,C_q\), such that, uniformly for
\(m\le k\le\lfloor\delta T\rfloor\), the following two geometries hold:
\[
 \Gamma_{T,m}\!\left((k/T)^\beta,C_Dk/(T-k)\right)\le C_0T/k,
 \tag{\text{slow channel}}
\]
and
\[
 c_0T/k^2\le
 \Gamma_{T,m}\!\left(C_H(k/T)^\beta,C_F\right)
 \le C_0T/k^2.
 \tag{\text{baseline-cancelled channel}}
\]
The slow-channel upper bound is attained by pooled one-date weights and has
exact energy \(2(Q_k^{-1}+R_k^{-1})\), where
\(Q_k=\sum_{g\le T-k}q_g\) and \(R_k=1-Q_k\).  The fast-channel upper bound
is attained by a data-driven coefficient array with \(w(a)=0\); it uses two
separated reverse-date blocks and the balancing equation
\(\sum_r A_r/R_r=0\).  Consequently one explicit affine procedure satisfies
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \left|\mathbb E_x[a^{\prime}Z]-\ell(x)\right|
 +\operatorname{sd}_x(a^{\prime}Z)
 \le C_0\min_{m\le k\le\lfloor\delta T\rfloor}
 \left[
 L(k/T)^\beta+\min\left\{
 \frac{Bk}{T-k}+\sigma\sqrt{\frac{T}{Nk}},
 B+\frac{\sigma\sqrt{T/N}}{k}
 \right\}\right].
\]
At the canonical equal-share sequence in the baseline-covariance obstruction
theorem, the slow-leverage constraints cannot be combined with energy of order
\(T/k^2\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency spine now uses the exact Pareto program and explicit covariance geometry, not the deleted lift handle or the diagnostic calendar formula.

proposed.statement:
Uniformly over the stated design range,
\[
 \frac{1-\frac12\sqrt{e-1}}8\,
 \omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2
 \le R^{\star}
 \le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \mathbb E_x\!\left[
 \{\widehat\theta_{r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}}-\ell(x)\}^2
 \right]
 \le\frac54\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2.
\]
Thus global minimax squared-error risk is comparable, with the displayed
numerical constants, to the exact modulus of the nested score operator.  The
candidate diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\), its minimizing depth \(k^{\star}\),
and a closed-form calendar phase diagram are not asserted to equal or be
equivalent to this exact modulus.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The theorem now depends only on the exact Gaussian experiment and total-modulus machinery; no unproved calendar-rate comparison remains in its proof spine.

proposed.statement:
For every \(j\in\mathbb N\), \(C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\) is a measurable interval
and satisfies
\[
 \inf_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \Pr_x\{\ell(x)\in C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
exactly.  Its half-length is within the factor \(1+j^{-1}\) of the infimum
over the positive-standard-deviation affine modulus intervals in the stated
construction.  Put
\[
 r_\alpha=\sqrt{\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\}},
 \qquad c_\alpha=\frac{(1-2\alpha)r_\alpha}{2},
 \qquad z_\alpha=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\]
Then
\[
 c_\alpha\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)
 \le\operatorname{EL}^{\star}_{\alpha}
 \le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
 \mathbb E_x[\operatorname{length}C_{\alpha,j}(Z)]
 \le(1+2z_\alpha)\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1).
\]
The lower bound ranges only over measurable interval-valued procedures, as in
the definition of \(\operatorname{EL}^{\star}_{\alpha}\).  No closed-form
calendar-rate equivalence is asserted.

prose_updates.tldr: Fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections induce an exact Gaussian not-yet-treated score experiment with a newly derived contemporaneous exhaustion term and a shared nested-baseline Gram term. The paper formulates the resulting baseline-cancellation Pareto program, proves pooled and baseline-cancelled feasible geometries, and gives an explicit equal-share certificate showing why small cohort-deviation leverage cannot be combined with the fast energy bound along a canonical growing-calendar sequence. Global minimax MSE and uniformly honest expected length are characterized, with explicit constants, by the exact nested covariance modulus. Converting that modulus into the candidate closed-form calendar functional remains open; the matched-date-block calculation applies only to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\).

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD work identifies effects only while valid comparisons remain, whereas Gaussian optimal-recovery work conditions on an already supplied operator and covariance. Neither literature derives the nested score covariance, separates contemporaneous exhaustion from shared-baseline cancellation, or studies the resulting coefficient Pareto frontier.
project_justification.niche: The paper treats late-calendar ATT inference as a growing, known-covariance Gaussian inverse problem. Its operator-specific content is the exact score covariance, the exposed affine coefficient program, two covariance geometries, and a rigorous obstruction to a tempting separable transport certificate.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the score law, defines a computable baseline-cancellation Pareto frontier, constructs pooled and baseline-cancelled affine channels, proves the fast-channel energy lower bound and a canonical baseline obstruction, and obtains exact-modulus minimax MSE and honest-length bounds. It leaves the matching intermediate Pareto lower bound, and therefore any closed calendar phase diagram, explicit as an open question.

sampling_model.design: Fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections at a common baseline and dates \(1,\ldots,T\), with cohort \(g\) treated from date \(g\) onward.
sampling_model.units: Independent Gaussian cohort-time cell means with known variance \(\sigma^2/(Nq_g)\) at each wave.
sampling_model.treatment: For each \(t\le T-m\), cohort \(g\le t\) is compared with the pooled set \(C_t\); no untreated cohort remains for the target at \(T\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed shares satisfy \(c_q/T\le q_g\le C_q/T\), so \(q_{>t}>0\) at every score date used by the experiment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated inside the exact Gaussian score experiment. Calendar smoothness and centered bounded cohort deviations determine worst-case affine bias through the explicitly defined leverage functionals \(H(a)\) and \(D(a)\).

prose_updates.related_work: Callaway and Sant'Anna provide the group-time causal effects and calendar aggregation underlying the target. Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess show why long-run event-study comparisons disappear, motivating extrapolation but not supplying its inference frontier. Sant'Anna and Zhao provide a two-period repeated-cross-section efficiency benchmark. Donoho's Gaussian modulus results and Armstrong and Kolesar's bias-aware interval theory supply generic optimal-recovery architecture once an operator and covariance are given; they do not derive the nested staggered-DiD score covariance or a bounded baseline-cancellation construction. Armstrong and Kolesar's direct-regression Holder calculations therefore do not establish the candidate nested calendar rate. Rambachan and Roth address sensitivity to untreated-trend violations rather than bounded heterogeneity of the treatment-effect surface. The matched-date-block calculation is a finite-sample calibration for \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\), not an ordering or rate transfer to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\).
prose_updates.interpretation: Two different uses of late score cells are now visible. Pooled one-date weights keep cohort-deviation bias small but retain shared-baseline noise; signed weights spread over separated reverse-date blocks can cancel that baseline term at the cost of constant cohort-deviation leverage. The exact nested modulus chooses over the full feasible geometry. The displayed candidate calendar functional records useful bias--variance scales, but it is not yet an identified closed form for that choice.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The matching lower interpolation of the baseline-cancellation Pareto frontier is not proved. In particular, the available obstruction rules out one four-inequality fast certificate along \(m=1\), \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\), but it neither rules out every bounded lift nor proves that the exact nested modulus is incomparable to every closed-form rate. Equal within-date marginals also do not order \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\) and \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\). The exact Gaussian analysis does not cover nuisance estimation or non-Gaussian approximation error.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved headline consists of the exact nested score covariance, the explicit coefficient-energy and bias map, the two feasible covariance geometries, the canonical baseline-Gram obstruction, and global MSE and interval-length bounds in terms of \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\). The candidate diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\), its minimizing depth, and the matched-date-block Holder rate are not transferred to the nested experiment. The intermediate Pareto interpolation and smoothness adaptation remain open-ended questions.
